pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/jobseeker/fetch/politeFetch.ts:232 When robots.txt cannot be reached (network error or timeout), the robots gate fails open and proceeds as allowed, so a hole in the gate's own vision reads as permission. The same function treats a 5xx as an outage that refuses (lines 220-222), and RFC 9309 treats unreachable as a full disallow.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/jobseeker/fetch/politeFetch.ts:232 Missing robots.txt is split correctly: 4xx, meaning no policy published (the subject's world), is allowed, and 5xx refuses. But a network failure is a gap in the instrument and is resolved as compliance. The warning is logged once and is not counted on any surface. politeFetch.test.ts:168 pins this behaviour.
app/_lib/jobseeker/rules/dsl.ts:41 The capture-group count comes from the regex engine itself, not from scanning the pattern text, and a pattern that fails to compile is refused.

app/_lib/jobseeker/rules/dsl.ts:64 The nested-quantifier scanner is not a parser, so it refuses the form it cannot clear. Its scope (model- or owner-authored rules) is code the system controls, which is the precondition the technique requires.
app/_lib/jobseeker/rules/dsl.ts:123 Each refusal names the rule index, the field and the fix (flatten it, or one of the listed values).
app/_lib/jobseeker/rules/engine.ts:196 The same check that validation runs is repeated at execution time, which catches rules stored before the gate existed.
app/_lib/jobseeker/rules/rules.test.ts:153 Six known-bad patterns are seeded and each must be refused, so the gate has been seen going red.

app/_lib/jobseeker/rules/collapse.ts:13 The collapse gate pauses a source only when a required rule yields nothing, or when an optional rule with an established baseline (≥5 matches) yields nothing. Rarely-matching optional fields cannot trip it.
